evaluations.verdict: The sturdiest pure-ring colour icon: one bold die-cut sticker on amber that stays a crisp rainbow C at 16px, handles dark mode cleanly, and brings the best functional idea in the round (a live notch that widens as the timer runs). But the notch, the concept's whole signature, is a 1px dent at tray size. The template collapses into a heavy donut that outweighs Wi-Fi and battery and reads as 'record' or 'O' rather than 'timer'.
evaluations.riff: Redraw the template at SF Symbols regular weight (ring about 12% of diameter). Deepen the spent notch into a clear wedge bridged by a 1.5pt track so the silhouette stays closed (no spinner read) but the notch survives at 16px and can animate as the live timer. Or plug the gap with starcap's star as the finish-line crown.

evaluations.verdict: The truest story in the set: the app's own hamster (checked against the reference, it's faithful) really does ride the leading cap, and at Dock size it reads as 'the rainbow timer with the runner'. It falls apart where the client needs it most. At 32/16 the hamster is a brown speck on a big empty dish, and the template is a thin/thick ring with a lump at the bottom that reads as a fishbowl or moon phase, not a hamster.
evaluations.riff: Make the hamster about three times larger and stand it on top of the ring at 12 o'clock, so its head and ears break the outer silhouette. The glyph then becomes a ring with a critter crown: a stopwatch at 18px, a hamster at 36px.

evaluations.verdict: The most complete system this round: the star gives the rainbow ring a focal point and a classroom meaning, the colour icon stays balanced down to 16px, and the template is the only one drawn at a weight that sits happily beside SF Symbols. At 18pt it reads as a stopwatch with its crown, exactly the right meaning for a tray item. Two weaknesses: the spent gap mostly hides under the star, so it reads as a full timer rather than a countdown, and the star is a generic gold star, not the app's orange sticker.
evaluations.riff: Swap in the app's actual orange star sticker (its gradient, thick white border, a tilt in 5° steps) and widen the spent gap to the left of the star (10 to 12 o'clock) so it still counts down. Enlarge the glyph's star by about 30% so its points survive at 18px @2x instead of becoming a nub.

evaluations.verdict: A friendly, toy-like colour icon that holds up at 16px, but the blocks look nothing like the app's smooth ring. The template is a dashed circle, which every Mac and GNOME user reads as a loading or sync spinner, the one thing a status item must not look like. It is also the rejected dot grid bent into a circle, and the hollow 'spent' socket turns to grey mush at 1x.
evaluations.riff: Use a solid ring for the resting mark and keep the segments only for the live running state (blocks drop out as time passes), so the menu-bar item never sits idle looking like a spinner.

evaluations.verdict: The most tasteful icon and the closest match to the sage, terracotta and rose UI, but it's the direction the client already rejected: nothing on it is what teachers see. The muted ring on deep sage loses contrast at 32/16, with visible conic-gradient streaks, and would flatten in tinted mode, where rose and sage have similar luminance. It reads as a meditation or budgeting app.
evaluations.riff: Don't ship it as a separate concept. Fold the palette into master as an alternate Dock icon (a settings toggle that sets NSApp.applicationIconImage) or as the dark variant, and raise the value contrast between rose and sage so it survives tinted mode and 16px.

evaluations.verdict: The most ownable, lovable Dock icon here: the hamster matches the app's own (orange oval body, tan head, round orange ears, dot eyes, curly tail), it pops in dark mode, and no other app has it. But the hamster now dominates the ring, so it reads 'pet app' before 'timer'. The template (a critter with eye holes, feet and tail inside a 250° open arc) clogs at 1x and flirts with a refresh arrow.
evaluations.riff: Simplify the template hamster to a solid silhouette (head, two ears and body; no eye holes, feet or tail curl). Close the arc into a full thin ring with a 1 to 1.5pt spent track, so it reads as 'creature in a timer' at 16px instead of a rotate/refresh icon.

evaluations.verdict: A faithful portrait of the name picker and the only idea that isn't a ring. But it copies a UI panel into a squircle, which the HIG warns against; the white chip with a black bar reads as a minus button or text field; and the rainbow timer the client asked for is gone. The boxed three-pill template is the heaviest glyph in the set and looks like a drawer, a server, or Control Center's toggles in the macOS menu bar.
evaluations.riff: Let the chosen chip break out of the reel: oversized, tilted and die-cut, overlapping the window frame, with confetti. The silhouette then becomes the 'picked!' moment instead of a UI card, and the glyph gets an ownable shape (a pill bursting through a frame) instead of a boxed list.

evaluations.verdict: It has the only ring that truly matches the in-app timer (timer.tsx's real conic gradient). But bolting a glossy traffic light onto the side makes two marks instead of the one the client asked for, pushes the composition off-centre and cools the palette. The template is an open C (reads as a spinner) plus a 3px pill whose lights collapse into a grey bar at 16 to 18px.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and give the true conic gradient, with the thinner in-app ring proportion, to the master/diecut sticker. If a second widget must appear, show it as colour (traffic-light green on the leading cap), not as a second object.

evaluations.verdict: Polished and the safest at 32/16, but it's the most generic ring in the set: a flat-banded rainbow donut that reads as a colour picker. The claimed 15° sticker tilt is invisible because a circle has no orientation. The template is a nearly solid disc with an irregular knockout, the heaviest ring glyph, and it reads as an eye or an appearance toggle next to the clock.
evaluations.riff: Give the die-cut a non-circular edge so it reads as a sticker: peel it up where time has been spent (a lifted, shadowed flap at the upper left). That also gives the glyph a distinctive flat-chord silhouette. Otherwise, merge it into master.

general: Eight of nine concepts are rings and seven share the same amber squircle; master, brandring and diecut are essentially one drawing. The ring is the right place to converge, since it's the most recognisable and scalable idea, but the thick hard-banded donut drifts toward colour-picker and Google territory and away from the app's thinner conic-gradient ring. The recurring failure is the menu-bar glyph: most are too heavy (master, brandring, diecut, reel) or too detailed (hamcap, mascot, ringplus), open arcs and dashed rings read as refresh or loading spinners, and only starcap pairs SF Symbols weight with a clear 'timer' meaning. Four things are missing from every sheet: the macOS 26 tinted and clear appearances (where the rainbow drops out and the silhouette has to carry identity), a plate-less die-cut version for Windows 11 and GNOME, a demo of master's live-progress glyph, and any nod to the name picker in the timer concepts. Next round should settle on one ring, add one ownable anchor at 12 o'clock (the app's real orange star versus the faithful hamster breaking the outline), draw the glyph at SF Symbols regular weight, and prototype the live countdown state; all nine followed the no-numerals and faithful-hamster rules, so no concept was penalised.

evaluations.verdict: This is the most system-ready mark in the set. The thick 250° band gives the best colour mass at 16/32 and in the favicon, and the die-cut notch keeps the white 16px tray glyph a single closed, heavy shape that no Wi-Fi, volume or spinner symbol shares; the widening-notch live state can be driven by Shell_NotifyIcon, AppIndicator and NSStatusItem alike. Weak spots: at 16px the notch is only a ~2px step, so the glyph drifts toward 'lumpy donut'; it is much heavier than Windows 11's 1px line tray icons; and the flat six-band palette reads a bit like Google next to a Google Classroom tab.
evaluations.riff: Hand-tune the tray glyph at 16, 20 and 24px: cut the notch as a clean step at least 3px deep and slim the band to ~3px, so it reads as a cut ring rather than a lump and sits closer to Fluent/GNOME stroke weight. Then ship the widening notch as the tray's running-timer state.

evaluations.verdict: At 128–256 it is the most literal picture of the running timer, and the hamster really is the app's own (so the rule is met). But everything it is about disappears below 48px: at 32/16 the rider is a brown smudge, and the thin ring leaves the favicon with little colour. The tray glyph is a 1–2px ring with a lump at the bottom, too light for GNOME symbolic, and it reads as something sitting in a bowl rather than a rider.
evaluations.riff: Merge with master using different art per size: master's thick notched ring and glyph at 16–32 and in the tray, with the hamster riding the leading cap only in the 48–256 .ico/.icns frames, where it can actually be seen.

evaluations.verdict: Warm and very classroom: a closed ring plus the gold-star sticker. It survives as a 16px favicon (ring plus yellow dot), and the star stays inside the maskable safe zone (it reaches 0.38 of the icon width; the limit is 0.40). In monochrome the star shrinks to a 2px bump at 12 o'clock, so the tray glyph is crisp and correctly weighted beside Windows/GNOME status icons but reads as a generic stopwatch crown (like Fluent's 'Timer' or SF Symbols' 'stopwatch'): easy to read, but not ownable.
evaluations.riff: Merge with master: move the star off 12 o'clock into master's spent-time notch (~10 o'clock). The colour icon keeps its gold star, and the glyph trades the stopwatch crown for master's ownable notched outline.

evaluations.verdict: A ring of six blobs is the universal busy/loading spinner. White on a dark taskbar at 16px it tells teachers the app is stuck, it is a close cousin of the dot grid the client wants gone, and the hollow 'spent' block dissolves into 1px mush. The colour icon keeps its dots of colour at 16px, but it reads as a colour wheel or a Trivial Pursuit pie, not the smooth timer ring teachers see.
evaluations.riff: Retire it. If the toy-block feel matters, fold it into master as faint seams on a continuous band, so the glyph stays one closed shape.

evaluations.verdict: Master's structure and identical glyph in the true brand colours: the best palette fit, and a sage plate that would stand out in a dock full of blue icons. But it is not what teachers see, and at 16px the sage-teal leading cap melts into the sage plate, so the ring becomes a muddy rose-brown donut chart that looks like a finance or wellness app. The deep plate also sinks on dark Windows taskbars and the GNOME dash.
evaluations.riff: Demote it to master's calm alternate (a dark-mode or in-app accent version). If it must lead, make the plate two steps lighter and push the leading cap to a pale sage-cream, so it separates from the plate at 16px and on dark taskbars.

evaluations.verdict: The strongest character icon here: at 48–256 the app's own hamster sitting in the rainbow ring is instantly the timer (rule met), and it would be memorable in a GNOME/KDE app grid. Below 32px it turns to mush, and the tray glyph is the wrong shape for a tray: an open, round-capped arc around a hamster blob reads as a refresh/history arrow (think Time Machine), and the 1px eye cut-outs fill in at 16px.
evaluations.riff: Keep the centred hamster for the 48–256 frames and the dock/app grid, but give the 16–32 sizes and the tray glyph to master's closed notched ring. The open arc has to go either way.

evaluations.verdict: The only concept that breaks away from the ring: the lilac-pink-butter slot card is clearly the name picker at 64+, the card stays just inside the 80% maskable circle (measured 0.398 of width, limit 0.40), and its glyph is the crispest in the set, snapped to the pixel grid at Windows 11 line weight. But at 16px the colour icon is a pink card with a minus sign, and the glyph's 1px outlined side pills read as a server, drawer or robot face: too thin for GNOME symbolic, and nothing says 'picker'.
evaluations.riff: Add the slot machine's pointer notches either side of the chosen chip and make the top and bottom pills solid 2px bars, so the 16px glyph reads as a picker rather than a server or filing cabinet.

evaluations.verdict: It has the most faithful ring (the real conic gradient from timer.tsx) plus a real widget, but the two-part layout halves both at 32/16, and the traffic light shrinks to a dark sliver. The tray glyph is the weakest in the set: an open C-shaped spinner beside a 3px dotted column that reads as 'O8' or a battery, right next to 'ENG 9:41'.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and give ringplus's genuine timer.tsx conic gradient to master's notched ring.

evaluations.verdict: Clean, heavy and closed: the solid die-cut disc makes a well-weighted GNOME-symbolic glyph, and the colour icon is the most literal timer widget (cream face, white rim, rainbow arc on amber). But it is also the most generic, a Google-coloured progress ring on a plate whose 15° tilt can't be seen on a circle, and at 16px the glyph reads as a donut or an eyeball rather than a timer.
evaluations.riff: On Windows and Linux, drop the plate and ship the round die-cut sticker itself (with its soft shadow) as an object-style icon, which both Fluent and GNOME prefer. Keep the amber plate only for macOS and the PWA maskable icon. That is the one thing it can do better than master.

general: Seven of the nine are the same rainbow ring on the same amber plate, so the colour side has converged; what really separates them is the 16px tray. There, only closed, single-shape outlines survive (master/brandring, starcap, diecut), and every added element (hamster, traffic light, blocks, side pills) collapses into a lump, a spinner or an 'O8'; no concept breaks the no-numerals or hamster rules. The flat red-orange-yellow-green-blue-purple bands appear in five concepts and look Google-ish at favicon size in a tab row full of Google Classroom and Drive; the app's own conic gradient, used only by ringplus, is a more ownable colour source. Missing entirely: different art per size (.ico and .icns frames can hold a different drawing at 16–32 than at 48–256, which is how to keep the hamster or star without wrecking small sizes), glyph weights per platform (1px line on Windows 11, 2px symbolic on GNOME, macOS template), plate-less object versions for Windows 11 and GNOME, and tray mock-ups beside real Wi-Fi/volume/battery icons and in Windows high-contrast mode. The next round should stop inventing new shapes: lock master's notched ring, hand-tune its glyph at 16/20/24px with a deeper notch, test the real conic gradient, use the hamster or star only as a large-size accent, and make the widening notch the tray's live running-timer state.

evaluations.verdict: The crispest glyph here and the only one that is not a ring, so it never collides with the clock, Time Machine, user-switching or record circles that already crowd a bar, and its framed three-pill stack matches the colour icon one-to-one. Its weak points are a generic rounded-square outline (all of its identity is on the inside) and a frame that is not snapped to whole pixels: at 16px@1x the outlined top and bottom pills go grey and the glyph collapses toward a minus-in-a-box, credit card or server-list icon.
evaluations.riff: Let the solid middle chip break out through the frame on both sides, so the silhouette itself says 'the picked name' and can never read as a minus-in-a-box. Make the top and bottom pills solid 1px stubs and pixel-fit the 16 and 18px drawings.

evaluations.verdict: The easiest ring in the set to spot: a heavy notched donut that is bolder than the thin system strokes, and at 18px and on Retina the upper-left shoulder gives it an outline the clock, user and record circles lack. But the glyph is the 1024-unit vector scaled down with no pixel-fitting, so at 16px@1x the 1px closure through the gap goes grey, and in a blur test it reads as a thick C with a hook at 9 o'clock (the refresh-arrow read it claims to avoid); with the rainbow gone, only the notch links it to the colour icon.
evaluations.riff: Ship pixel-fitted 16 and 18px drawings: a solid 2px band through the gap, the two shoulders squared into single crisp 1px steps, and the hole snapped to whole pixels. Then build the live widening notch, because a spent-time wedge is one of the few states still readable at 16px.

evaluations.verdict: The cleanest outline here: a 2px ring that sits well on the pixel grid at 16 and 18px, with nothing muddy. But the star is only about 3x2px at 1x, so it becomes a nub and the glyph reads as a generic stopwatch (a close relative of the clock and power symbols), which says 'some timer app' rather than this app; the star only becomes a star on Retina.
evaluations.riff: Make the star big enough to survive, about 40% of the glyph width, cut into the ring at 12 with a 1px gap, so a five-point shape is still there at 16px. Or seat it in master's notch so the outline has both a notch and a star.

evaluations.verdict: The only glyph with a face: the cut-out eyes make it read at once as a critter, and nothing in any tray looks like it, so it is genuinely ownable. At 16-18px@1x, though, the hamster is a 7x6px lump with 1px ears and grey eyes, and the open 250-degree arc with the head poking into the gap reads as a circular arrow (a relative of Time Machine and refresh); until Retina it looks like a generic pig, cat or bird rather than the app's hamster.
evaluations.riff: Close the arc into a full ring to remove the arrow read. Let the hamster's head and two round ears break out through the ring's upper-left edge so they become bumps on the outline that survive at 16px, and ship a pixel-fitted small drawing with no eye cut-outs below 20px.

evaluations.verdict: The glyph is identical to master's, so it gets the same verdict: an easy-to-spot heavy notched donut that blurs into a hooked C at 16px@1x. What changes is the colour icon the glyph points back to: the rose-to-sage ring on deep sage is the lowest-contrast icon at 16px and not what teachers see on the board, so the link from menu bar to Dock is weaker.
evaluations.riff: Use it as master's dark-appearance or brand-collateral variant rather than a separate mark. If it stays primary, lighten the sage leading cap so the end of the arc keeps its contrast against the plate at 16px.

evaluations.verdict: The boldest closed outline (a perfect heavy disc that can never become a C), but that outline carries no identity: the ring caps that define the concept end up as two lumps on the inner edge, and they go grey at 16px@1x. At a glance it reads as a record button, an eyeball or a moon-in-a-circle night-mode icon, and it is the heaviest ink blot in any bar.
evaluations.riff: Move the identity to the outside: let the die-cut edge step in along the spent gap (master's notch), or cut one clean wedge through the border there. Either way it effectively becomes master.

evaluations.verdict: At 16-18px@1x it is a thin ring with a 5x3px blob at the bottom, which reads as macOS's person-in-circle user-switching icon (or a fishbowl), and the heavier right-hand arc adds a generic progress-ring read. It only becomes a sweet hamster-in-a-wheel on Retina, and the colour icon has the same scale problem: the runner is a brown smudge by 32px.
evaluations.riff: Scale the rider up to about 45% of the glyph and move it onto the rim at 7 o'clock, so its head and ears break the ring's outer edge and become part of the outline instead of a blob inside it. Use one 2px ring weight instead of the thin-plus-heavy pair.

evaluations.verdict: Two unrelated shapes side by side: at 16px@1x the open arc reads as a refresh spinner, and the 2x5px traffic-light pill loses its dots and becomes a battery or an 'i', so the pair reads like text ('Oi') rather than one mark. Shrinking the ring to make room for the pill leaves it only about 11px tall, visibly smaller than the glyphs around it, and the colour icon is just as crowded at 16px.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light from both the glyph and the icon and give the whole glyph box to a closed ring. The real timer gradient it uses can carry on as master's colour treatment instead.

evaluations.verdict: At every true size this is the dashed-circle or activity-spinner glyph that means 'loading' or 'not started', and next to a gear it reads as a cog. The one hollow 'spent' block turns into a grey 1px smudge at 16px, erasing the only idea that sets it apart, and a ring of six blobs is the same dot-cluster genre as the 3x3 grid the client wants gone.
evaluations.riff: Retire it as a tray mark. If the toy-block idea stays, fuse the five lit blocks into one continuous arc with shallow seam notches and make the spent block a real gap, which turns it into master's notched ring.

general: Seven of the nine glyphs are rings, and a real menu bar already has rings in it (clock, Time Machine, user switching, record/stop, progress), so a glyph's identity has to live in its outline (a notch, a bump or a break-out), because detail inside the shape disappears first; master's notch and reel's framed stack are the only ideas that still read at 16px@1x. No concept has a pixel-fitted small glyph: every tray glyph is the same 1024-unit vector scaled to 16 and 18px, and the grey 1px strokes that result wipe out exactly the detail each idea depends on (master's gap closure, reel's pills, starcap's star, mascot's ears and eyes, segments' spent block, diecut's caps), while stroke weight swings from heavy ink blots (diecut, master) to thin wires (starcap, hamcap). The next round should hand-fit 16 and 18px drawings for each glyph, test them with a blur/squint check beside real system icons, build the live countdown state, and try one merge: master's notched ring with the app hamster's head and ears peeking out of the spent gap, so the timer and the mascot share one outline that no system icon has. No concept broke the no-numerals rule, and both hamster concepts use the app's own hamster.

evaluations.verdict: This is the strongest all-rounder and the best system idea in the round. The die-cut 'bite' where spent time is cut away gives the rainbow ring a stepped, closed silhouette that works in one colour, holds up at 16px on every bar, and could become a live signature (the menu-bar notch drains with the class timer). The risk is that a flat red-to-violet donut sits in Google's and Time Timer's visual territory, so at tab size the amber plate and the bite do all of the differentiating.
evaluations.riff: Merge with mascot. Keep this exact notched sticker and its glyph, and put the app's hamster in the bite, running along the thin border from the violet cap towards twelve. The notch then reads as the hamster's path (it 'ate' the spent time), and the silhouette gains a creature no competitor can own while the tray glyph stays a bold notched ring.

evaluations.verdict: This is the truest scene (the creature running the rainbow ring is exactly what a class points at), but it is too timid to be a mark: the thin, airbrushed ring around a big cream face reads as a dinner plate, the hamster is only a quarter of the ring's width and turns into a brown smudge by 32px, and the tray glyph becomes a porthole with a lump in it.
evaluations.riff: Use master's thick, hard-jointed band and notch, and scale the hamster up about 1.6x so it straddles the leading cap and breaks the outer silhouette. Drop the soft colour blend, which edges towards Copilot-style gradient loops.

evaluations.verdict: Polished and friendly, but the least ownable idea: a nearly closed primary-colour ring is Chrome and Google Photos territory, a gold star is every edu brand's reward shorthand (and the app's own star sticker is orange, not gold), and in the tray it shrinks to the standard stopwatch icon, which is very legible and belongs to nobody.
evaluations.riff: Replace the gold star with the app's own orange die-cut star, made bigger and slapped across the ring at 1–2 o'clock instead of perched at 12. It then reads as a sticker rather than a stopwatch button, and the glyph gets an off-centre bump that is ownable.

evaluations.verdict: The toy-block idea is fun, but what renders is a colour wheel: pink, orange, yellow, green and blue blocks plus a beige empty socket look like a Trivial Pursuit pie or a Photos-style pinwheel, they replace the continuous ring teachers actually see, and the tray glyph is a dashed circle, the standard 'loading' spinner and the worst possible meaning for a menu-bar item.
evaluations.riff: Join the blocks into one continuous band with thin seams on master's notched silhouette, so it reads as the app's timer and the glyph becomes a solid ring rather than a spinner.

evaluations.verdict: The most grown-up option and the one closest to the brand palette, and deep sage is rare among edu marks. But it gives away the one thing teachers recognise (the rainbow on amber) and turns into a wellness or fintech 'sunset donut', and a green tile next to Google Classroom's green in a teacher's tab bar is a real confusion risk.
evaluations.riff: Don't ship it as the app icon. Make it the identity's secondary voice instead: master's shape in brand enamel for docs, website headers, print and slides, while the rainbow master stays the app icon, so both share one silhouette.

evaluations.verdict: The most ownable and memorable mark here. None of the listed competitors has a character (ClassDojo shows teachers bond with one), the hamster in the ring reads instantly as a hamster-wheel timer, and the app's six-creature cast gives the identity years of use in docs, marketing and seasonal variants. The weak link is the tray: a full-body silhouette inside an open 250° arc is mush at 16px on Windows and GNOME, and the open arc looks a bit like a refresh arrow.
evaluations.riff: Redraw the glyph as master's closed, notched sticker outline with the hamster knocked out of the face, so it never reads as a refresh arrow. Hand-tune a 16/18px hamster (body, one ear, eye, thick tail, no feet), and avoid a head-and-two-ears glyph, which reads as Mickey Mouse.

evaluations.verdict: The only concept that breaks away from the rings, with the crispest tray glyph of the round, and teachers who use the name picker will know it straight away. But a framed card in a square is one of the most common app-icon shapes, the name shrunk to a dark bar reads as a minus or eject button, the glyph looks like a filing cabinet or server rack to anyone who doesn't know the app, and it drops the rainbow timer that teachers mention first.
evaluations.riff: Draw the reel as a curved drum, with the neighbouring names foreshortened and dimmed towards the top and bottom and two payline arrows pointing at the chosen name. It then reads as a slot machine rather than a stack of drawers, and the arrows give the glyph a cue no cabinet icon has.

evaluations.verdict: This is a screenshot collage rather than a mark: the real neon gradient from timer.tsx lands squarely in the Copilot and Apple Intelligence 'AI halo' look, the vertical traffic light is a generic street signal (the app's own is a horizontal pill), the layout is lopsided and the least warm of the set, and at 16px the glyph reads as 'O8' or a refresh arrow next to a battery.
evaluations.riff: Take the traffic light out of the mark and keep it for feature illustrations. If a second widget has to appear, fold it into the ring as three small red, amber and green dots sitting in the spent gap, so there is one silhouette.

evaluations.verdict: The most faithful timer-as-sticker (pale spent track, round caps, thick white border) and clean at 32 and 16px, but a tilted circle looks exactly like an untilted one, so the only sticker cue is the white rim, and the plain round silhouette leaves nothing to own: at tab size it is a white disc with a primary-colour ring, close to Chrome.
evaluations.riff: Fold it into master: cut the die-cut border to follow the ring's caps (the notch) so the silhouette carries the idea, and keep this version's pale spent track inside the notch as the cue from the app.

general: Seven of the nine concepts are the same rainbow ring on an amber plate with small add-ons, and a ring on its own is standard for the category (Time Timer's disc, Apple's Activity rings, Google's primary-colour Chrome and Photos marks). So only two things in this round are truly ownable at 16px: master's die-cut 'bite' silhouette and the app's own hamster. All nine follow the no-numerals rule, and both hamster concepts use the real creature faithfully. The flat, hard-jointed bands taken from the rainbow sticker are the right colour choice, because the real neon gradient (ringplus, and hamcap's airbrushed blend) drifts into the Copilot and Apple Intelligence 'AI halo' look. What's missing is any proof the mark can carry an identity beyond the dock: there is no wordmark lockup, no one-colour print or stamp version, no test in macOS tinted/clear modes or as an Android themed icon (where the rainbow disappears and only the silhouette is left), no animation frames for the live notch, and only the reel covers the 'name picker' half of the brief. The next round should push a master and mascot merge (the notched die-cut ring with the hamster breaking the silhouette in the bite), with a hand-drawn 16/18px glyph that doesn't read as a refresh arrow, a spinner or Mickey Mouse ears, shown with a lockup and a tinted-mode test; brandring's palette should become the identity's secondary voice rather than a rival icon.

evaluations.verdict: Bold, cheerful, and one of the strongest at 16px, but my first thought was 'rainbow bagel with a bite out of it'. Six flat stripes on a white plate look more like a donut chart or a Google product than my smooth, glowing timer, and the cut-away makes the red cap bulge out at twelve like a fat comma. The glyph is clean and closed, but at true 16px the notch is barely visible and it reads as a slightly lopsided thick O.
evaluations.riff: Swap the six hard stripes for the timer's smooth conic gradient and sit the app's hamster on the leading purple cap (hamcap's idea), so the cut-away reads as the path the hamster has already run.

evaluations.verdict: This is the one that made me say 'oh, that's the timer': a smooth rainbow ring with our actual hamster riding the end of it, exactly like my board. A ring with a critter at the bottom also reads as a hamster in a wheel, which is a lovely pun, and the glyph keeps that read even at true 16px. The problem is that the hamster is tiny and tucked at 7 o'clock on a huge empty plate, so at 32px it's an orange crumb and at 16px it's gone.
evaluations.riff: Scale the hamster up about 1.6x and move it to 6 o'clock so it's clearly running inside a wheel. Thicken the ring toward master's weight, and drop the knocked-out eye from the 16/18px glyph so the silhouette stays a clean blob.

evaluations.verdict: The gold star is pure classroom, and that's exactly the problem: it says reward chart or behaviour points, not timer. Sitting on top of a nearly full ring, it looks like an engagement ring or a wreath before it looks like a countdown, and it isn't even the app's orange star. The glyph is crisp and reads as a stopwatch, which fits a timer but looks like every other timer icon.
evaluations.riff: Use the app's own orange star sticker at twice the size, with a visible tilt and a white die-cut border, and open a real spent gap beside it so the ring reads as a countdown rather than jewellery.

evaluations.verdict: The toy colours are cheerful and look lovely on the amber board, but I'd guess 'baby toy' or 'Trivial Pursuit wheel', not my timer, which is one continuous glowing ring. The tray glyph is a textbook loading spinner: in my menu bar it would look like something had frozen mid-lesson, and that rules it out.
evaluations.riff: Join the blocks edge-to-edge into one continuous band with a single recessed spent socket, so the glyph is a closed ring with one notch and can never be mistaken for a spinner.

evaluations.verdict: Tasteful and grown-up. If I saw it in the staffroom I'd assume it was a mindfulness or budgeting app. It drains out the rainbow, which is the one thing teachers recognise, the band turns muddy olive in the middle, and on the real amber canvas it's the only tile that looks like it belongs to another product.
evaluations.riff: Fold it into master as the dark-appearance variant only. The main icon needs the amber plate and the real rainbow that teachers actually see.

evaluations.verdict: This got the biggest smile from me: our actual hamster, big and centred, warm and trustworthy, and my students would point at it in the dock. The hamster survives at 32px and 16px better than any other detail in the set, though the whole thing leans towards 'kids' pet game' and the thin ring reads more as a frame than a countdown. The glyph is the weak half: at true 16px the hamster mushes into a cat-or-pig blob inside an open arc that reads as refresh/sync, uncomfortably close to Time Machine's icon.
evaluations.riff: Keep this colour icon but borrow hamcap's tray solution: a closed ring with a solid, simplified hamster silhouette (head, two ear bumps, body, no knocked-out eyes) sitting at the bottom like a hamster in a wheel.

evaluations.verdict: The lilac-to-pink card is clearly our name picker, and it's the only tile that wouldn't disappear in a row of rainbow rings. Out of context, though, the white chip with a black dash reads as a minus button or a toaster slot, the two confetti flecks look like crumbs, and the rainbow timer is gone entirely. The glyph is the crispest at true 1x, but it reads as a filing cabinet or a server and looks a bit like the macOS Control Center toggles.
evaluations.riff: Replace the single black dash with two short bars of unequal length (the shape of a first name), tilt the chosen chip like a die-cut sticker, and give it a proper burst of 5-6 confetti flecks so the moment reads as 'picked!' rather than 'minus'.

evaluations.verdict: I recognise both widgets. It's the only concept using the timer's real smooth gradient, and I use the traffic light every lesson. Squeezed together, though, they look like a camera lens with a flash, and the lopsided layout feels like a dashboard rather than a mark. At 16px the traffic light is a dark speck, and the glyph at true size reads as a broken O next to a battery, like 'O8'.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light entirely and give the timer's smooth gradient to master or hamcap, which need it more than this layout needs a second widget.

evaluations.verdict: Clean, confident, and the boldest browser-tab icon in the set. But a 15° tilt is invisible on a circle, so the sticker idea only comes through the white rim and shadow, and it mostly reads as a donut chart on a paper plate: safe and forgettable. The glyph is the heaviest and most visible tray mark, but at 16px the lumpy inner edge looks like a rendering glitch rather than time already spent.
evaluations.riff: Make the die-cut non-circular so the tilt and the sticker both read. Let the white border bulge around a hamster riding the leading cap (a merge with hamcap), like the app's own stickers, whose borders follow their outline.

general: Seven of the nine are the same rainbow donut with a different topping. Drawn as six hard stripes on a white plate (master, starcap, diecut), they look more like a donut chart, a Google-palette product or a flag than the app's smooth, glowing timer; the concepts that used the real gradient felt far more like 'our timer'. The hamster is the strongest recognition and warmth cue in the whole set: both hamster concepts pass the likeness rule, and none of the nine uses numerals. Round 4 should commit to hamster plus ring and solve its two open problems: a hamster big enough to survive 32px and 16px, and a closed, simple tray silhouette, where hamcap's accidental 'hamster in a wheel' is the best glyph idea so far. Drop open arcs and dashed rings from the glyphs, since they read as refresh, Time Machine or loading. Still missing is a demo of the live menu-bar glyph draining during a countdown, which would really help a teacher glancing up mid-lesson, and the reel deserves one more pass as the name-picker alternative.

evaluations.verdict: The most accessible system here. A continuous white disc encloses every band, so the rainbow never touches bare amber (where red vs amber collapses to ΔE 4 under deutan), and the 16px favicon still shows the app's actual rainbow C on white. Its glyph is the only one that stays a single crisp, closed piece at true 16 and 18px (64–78px counter, 27–35% grey pixels, confident weight). The weakness: the spent bite lives in the counter, not the outer edge, so at 16px it reads as a thick ring with a lumpy hole more than a timer running down.
evaluations.riff: Merge with master: deepen the bite so the thin wall is exactly 2px and the counter steps by at least 2px at 16px, then adopt master's live widening-notch menu-bar state. That keeps diecut's closure and gains master's readable countdown.

evaluations.verdict: The best-measured tray glyph in the set: at true 16px it carries 40% ink, has an 8px counter and only 13–22% of its ink falls under 3:1. The thick-to-thin step sits on the outer edge, so 'drained ring' reads with no colour at all. Its weak spot is the 1px closing bridge, which renders at 33–70% alpha and breaks at 16px, so on a light Windows taskbar it drifts toward a heavy C. In colour, the white die-cut outline is load-bearing, because red and green bands against bare amber are only ΔE 4–10 under deutan/protan.
evaluations.riff: Draw the notch bridge at a full 2px (128 units) in hand-tuned 16/18px masters so the silhouette really stays closed, and keep the white die-cut outline at every size, 16px included.

evaluations.verdict: The most legible glyph in the set: a 2px ring with 28% ink (closest to system-icon weight) and one large counter. At 1x, though, the star shrinks to a 3px nub and the mark reads as a generic stopwatch, not this app. In colour, its one distinguishing element depends on hue: the gold star is only 1.65:1 against its white border and 1.8:1 against the amber plate, so in greyscale or on a washed-out projector it nearly vanishes.
evaluations.riff: Give the star a dark amber keyline (at least 3:1 on white), and enlarge the glyph's star to about 40% of the width so it reads as a star at 16px rather than a stopwatch crown.

evaluations.verdict: The hamster is faithful to the app's creature and follows the rule. Drawn this large, it is the only character that still reads as a creature in the 16px colour icon. The glyph falls apart at true 16px: the 1px eyes, ears and tail turn to noise (44% grey pixels), leaving a lumpy cat-or-bird blob inside an open arc that reads as a reload arrow. In the dark variant, the brown outline is only 1.3–1.6:1 against the dark face and the orange body about 2.8:1.
evaluations.riff: Close the arc into a heavy ring to kill the reload read, and hand-hint a 16px hamster with 2px eyes, fused paws and a thicker tail. Lighten the dark-mode outline to tan so the body edge clears 3:1.

evaluations.verdict: At 256px and up it is the most literal picture of the app, and the hamster follows the rule. At true 16px the 64-unit rim turns into a broken 1px grey line (21–25% of ink under 3:1 on light bars) and the rider shrinks to a 3–4px lump with a 1px eye, so the glyph reads as a fishbowl and the favicon as an empty cream disc. The rider also has no luminance edge: the orange body on the violet band is 1.5:1, so once the brown outline drops out it merges into the ring in greyscale.
evaluations.riff: Park the hamster on the pale spent track instead of the violet cap (orange on cream is 3.4:1), raise the glyph rim to at least 2px, and let sizes of 32px and below fall back to master's heavy ring.

evaluations.verdict: The content most robust to colour blindness in the set: the chosen name is carried by luminance (white chip, 12.3:1 dark bar, faded neighbours), so it survives protan, deutan, tritan and greyscale, and it is the only non-circular silhouette. The glyph undercuts this. The 84-unit frame isn't pixel-snapped at 16px (65% of its ink is grey), the outlined neighbour pills fill in, and what's left reads as ⊟ (collapse). At 47% ink in a full square it also looms over the Wi-Fi and battery icons, and the card corners slightly overrun the 80% maskable circle.
evaluations.riff: Pixel-snap a dedicated 16px glyph: a 1px frame inset to 14px, the solid chip, and the neighbours as short 1px dashes instead of outlined pills, so it reads as a reel window rather than a minus box.

evaluations.verdict: It shares master's glyph, so its tray legibility is identical (good), and white on deep sage (11.4:1) is the strongest figure-ground in the set. But the palette sits exactly on the red-green confusion axis. Terracotta and sage have identical luminance (1.0:1), the band spans only L* 53–66, and for protanopes its two ends are just ΔE 9 apart, so the warm-to-cool band becomes one khaki smear. At 16px it looks muddy even to typical vision, and losing the rainbow and the amber canvas kills recognition.
evaluations.riff: Keep the rainbow ring and use deep sage only for the plate, or rebuild the band as a lightness ramp (pale rose to deep teal, at least 3:1 end to end) so the progression survives colour blindness.

evaluations.verdict: Two widgets in 16px is one too many. The glyph is only 14×11px at 16px, so it looks undersized next to its neighbours; its open C reads as a spinner or reload arrow, the traffic-light pill as a battery or an '8', and the three lamps are 1px holes. In colour, the traffic light's state survives red-green colour blindness only through the lit lamp's lightness (4.4:1 over the unlit red), and at 16px the lamps are single pixels anyway.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light from the glyph and from icons at 32px and below. Keep it only at 128px and up, with the lit lamp also drawn larger, so its state never depends on hue.

evaluations.verdict: Fails both of my core tests. The glyph is six separate blobs with one fainter: the universal loading spinner at every size (7 fragments and 31–40% of ink under 3:1 at 16px), and uncomfortably close to the dot grid the client wants gone. In colour, which block is spent depends on hue: the yellow block against the empty socket is 1.18:1 (ΔE 6 in greyscale), and pink and green drop to about ΔE 30 under deutan. Once the recess shading is lost at 16px, a low-vision or colour-blind teacher sees two empty blocks.
evaluations.riff: Fuse the blocks into one continuous band with hairline seams, make the spent slot a true cut to the plate (a change in silhouette, not a pale fill), and deepen the yellow to amber so every lit block is at least 1.8:1 against cream.

general: Seven of nine concepts are the same rainbow ring, and their accessibility depends on one element: the white die-cut rim. Bare rainbow on amber collapses for red-green colour blindness (red vs plate is ΔE 4 under deutan; luminance is 1.1–1.3:1), so the rim must be a fixed spec at every size. No element that carries meaning should depend on hue, yet starcap's star (1.65:1), segments' spent block (1.18:1) and hamcap's rider (1.5:1) all do. How well a glyph survives in the tray tracks how simple its silhouette is: only the single closed heavy rings (diecut, master and brandring's copy) stay intact at true 16px. Every 1px feature (hamster eyes, lamp holes, outlined pills, hairline rims) turns to grey fuzz, and four glyphs collide with system meanings (spinner, reload, stopwatch, ⊟). Missing across the set: hand-hinted 16px masters for Windows at 100% and GNOME (most glyphs are tuned at 18/36px and merely scaled down), and any test of the tray's live running and idle states. Next round: converge on diecut/master with a closing wall of at least 2px, prototype master's widening-notch idea as a live 16px state, and keep the hamster to 64px and up and to in-app moments rather than the tray.

evaluations.verdict: This is the only concept whose silhouette carries an idea: the spent time is literally cut out of the sticker. The caps and notch fillets are cleanly resolved, the light comes consistently from the top left, the 32/16 small masters are excellent, and the glyph could animate live without numerals. What lets it down is the six hard-jointed bands, which read as a pie chart or colour picker rather than the app's thin neon ring. There is also a cool mint track in the notch, and the glyph is heavy and lopsided, with the bite shrinking to a bump at 16 px.
evaluations.riff: Keep the notch. Replace the six Google-ish hard bands with a warm continuous sweep based on the app's real ring gradient. Hand-hint the glyph at 16/18 px with a deeper, squarer bite and a slightly lighter weight so the notch reads as deliberate.

evaluations.verdict: This is the truest snapshot of the classroom board, and the hamster is faithful. At icon scale, though, it is a small critter perched on the inside edge of a big white plate, it becomes a brown smudge by 32 px, and a hamster inside a circle reads as a 'hamster wheel' (the daily grind) rather than a countdown. In the glyph, the hairline outer ring goes grey and the hamster becomes a lump at 16–18 px.
evaluations.riff: Fold it into mascot. If the rider idea survives, double the hamster to about 40% of the ring diameter and seat it on the outside of the leading cap, as in the app. Make the glyph master's plain notched ring with no creature.

evaluations.verdict: It is crisp and well lit, and it has the most legible tray mark in the set. But it is a gold-star reward cliché pinned to a pie-chart ring, and the star is not even the app's own sticker, which is orange. In monochrome the star shrinks to a nub, so the glyph becomes a generic stopwatch, and at 150 px it looks like a diamond ring.
evaluations.riff: Swap the gold star for the app's orange star sticker and let it ride the leading cap as the runner instead of crowning 12 o'clock. That way it earns its place, and the glyph stops reading as a stopwatch or an engagement ring.

evaluations.verdict: Toy blocks are a fresh thought, and the icon feels tactile, with consistent corner radii and believable lighting on the recessed socket. But no ring of blocks exists anywhere in the app, and pink has replaced red, so recognition drops. Worse, the glyph is a dashed circle, the universal loading/busy spinner, and its hollow socket turns to mush at 16 px.
evaluations.riff: Close the ring back up. Keep the chunky toy feel but join the blocks into master's continuous band with seams only. Treat the spent socket as the notch, filled solid in the glyph, so the tray mark is a closed ring with one bite rather than a spinner.

evaluations.verdict: It has the most grown-up palette and inherits master's good silhouette and glyph. But the rose-to-sage gradient passes through a muddy olive, the sage leading cap has little contrast against the deep sage plate, and faint radial striations show in the gradient at 64 px. Without the amber or the rainbow, it looks like a wellness app rather than the board teachers see.
evaluations.riff: Demote it to master's macOS dark/tinted appearance instead of a standalone mark. Use the brand enamels in stepped, hard-jointed bands with no muddy blend, and put terracotta on the leading cap for contrast.

evaluations.verdict: This is the most ownable and recognisable mark in the set. The app's exact hamster, at home in the rainbow ring, instantly says 'the timer with the hamster' and still reads as an orange critter at 16 px. The craft problems are a heavy cream halo around the plate and a cramped face where the head and tail crowd the ring. The glyph, a critter with eye holes inside an open arc, becomes a noisy blob in a refresh loop at 16–18 px.
evaluations.riff: Merge with master. Seat the hamster, about 10% smaller for breathing room, inside master's notched die-cut ring, and drop the plate halo. Make the tray glyph master's notched ring without the creature, so the icon keeps the character and the glyph stays legible and matching.

evaluations.verdict: It is a faithful, well-built randomiser card and the only genuinely different subject in the set. But with the names reduced to a black bar, it reads as a minus sign in a form field. The squircle-in-squircle framing and the two stray confetti flecks feel generic, and the framed three-pill glyph looks like a stock server or drawer icon, with its inner shapes filling in at 16 px.
evaluations.riff: Crop in hard so the gradient reel window bleeds to the plate edge, with no cream card frame. Add slot-machine pointer notches on either side of a bolder chosen chip so it reads as 'picked' rather than 'minus', and drop the frame from the glyph.

evaluations.verdict: It feels like a committee collage. The ring, which usefully uses the app's real conic gradient, is pushed off-centre by a glossy, skeuomorphic vertical traffic light, while the app's traffic light is horizontal. Two rendering styles and two subjects end up fighting for 16 px. The glyph is an open C (a refresh arrow) beside a dotted bar, and together they read as 'O8' or a battery.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light entirely and carry its one good decision, the app's real ring gradient, into master's notched sticker ring.

evaluations.verdict: It is clean, closed and robust at every size, and it keeps the app's timer face and track. But it is the safest possible statement: a plain disc in the donut-chart/Activity-ring genre. The claimed 15° tilt is invisible on a circle, and the heavy bevelled rim looks like a porcelain plate rather than a paper sticker. The knockout glyph is bold but ambiguous; it could be an eye, a record or a progress spinner.
evaluations.riff: Make the die-cut visible. Give the sticker a non-circular outline at the spent gap (master's notch or a lifted, peeling edge), and flatten the rim to paper white so the tilt and the sticker quality actually come through.

general: Seven of the nine concepts are the same rainbow donut on an amber plate with different garnish, so the round converged too early. The only real differentiators are master's notch, which puts the idea in the silhouette and allows a live menu-bar glyph, and mascot's hamster, the one truly ownable asset. Nearly every concept borrowed the rainbow sticker's six hard bands, which reads as a pie chart, colour picker or Google logo rather than the app's thin neon ring; nobody has yet found a warm, ownable colour treatment for the ring. Every glyph that adds a second element (hamster, star, traffic light, frame, hollow socket) falls apart at 16–18 px, while the closed, single-idea silhouettes survive. Next round should lock master's notched die-cut ring as the shared silhouette for icon and glyph, test the verbatim hamster inside it on the colour icon only, push a less generic ring palette, and hand-tune the glyph pixel by pixel at 16/18/20 px. The name picker, which the client named, deserves one stronger attempt that keeps a visible 'chosen' moment.

evaluations.verdict: The strongest system here because the idea is a rule rather than a picture: spent time is cut out of the die-cut sticker, so one silhouette can serve as dock icon, a live tray glyph whose notch widens, a countdown favicon and a self-drawing loader. The static drawing lags the idea, though: the border pinches into small kinks where it wraps the round caps, the flat hard-joined bands read more donut chart than the app's glowing gradient ring, and at true 16px the 110° notch shrinks to mere lopsidedness, so the idle glyph reads as a heavy O.
evaluations.riff: Redraw the die-cut as a constant-width offset with no pinch at the caps, lighten the glyph band about 25% to sit at SF Symbol weight, and prove the live notch with a 16/18px idle, 25, 50, 75 and zero state strip.

evaluations.verdict: Through a motion lens this is the app's own animation paused on one frame, and the orbiting hamster gives the best loading and live-tray idea in the set (a bump that travels round the glyph as time runs). The frame chosen is weak: the faithful hamster is tiny, parked on the violet cap at 7 o'clock under a big empty cream face, so the icon feels bottom-heavy and quiet; it becomes a brown smudge at 16px, and the glyph reads as a lump in a fishbowl.
evaluations.riff: Make it the running state of mascot rather than a standalone icon: ship mascot's hamster-at-home as the static mark, and use this rider pose for the loading loop and the live tray glyph, where the hamster bump orbits the ring as time runs.

evaluations.verdict: The most dependable tray mark: at true 1x the ring with a nub reads instantly as a stopwatch on every bar, and the fixed star gives a live draining glyph a readable finish line, with a built-in payoff (the star pops and sheds confetti at zero) that suits gold-star classroom culture. The colour icon is pleasant but generic, since a flat six-band ring with a star topper reads as a wreath or a jewelled ring, and the glyph's strength (it looks like a stopwatch) is also its weakness (so does every timer app's).
evaluations.riff: Give the ring master's die-cut notch so its outline is ownable, keep the star fixed at 12 as the finish-line anchor for the live glyph, and use the app's own orange star sticker rather than a new gold one.

evaluations.verdict: The only concept whose live tray states are legible by design (six blocks down to zero, each state clear at 16px), and the toy-block bounce is a fun motion idea. At rest, though, the glyph is a dashed circle, the universal loading/syncing spinner, which is the wrong message for an idle tray item; the colour icon reads as a colour wheel or Trivial Pursuit pie rather than the continuous timer teachers see, and the recessed spent socket is gone below 32px.
evaluations.riff: Close the ring at rest: draw one continuous band with engraved seams so the idle glyph is a solid ring, and break it into discrete blocks only while a timer is actually live.

evaluations.verdict: Calm, handsome, and the only concept in the brand UI palette, but as a system it is a palette swap of master rather than a new idea, and it throws away the two signals teachers actually recognise (the rainbow and the amber board). The muted gradient also loses contrast at 16px, where the sage-teal leading cap sinks into the sage plate, and the glyph inherits master's heavy, lumpy idle state unchanged.
evaluations.riff: Keep it as master's brand/tinted variant (marketing site, print, the macOS tinted appearance) and leave the product icon rainbow-on-amber.

evaluations.verdict: The richest system in the set: the app's hamster (faithful, and already built in calm and shocked states) supplies idle, time's-up, loading (running in its rainbow wheel) and empty-state (napping in the ring) poses for free, so the brand gets a performer rather than just a logo, and the icon is warm and unmistakable in a dock. The tray is the weak link, because at 16px the open arc plus a blob with eye holes reads as a rotate arrow wrapped round a pig or cat, the busiest glyph on any bar.
evaluations.riff: Close the glyph's arc with a thin spent track so it stops reading as rotate/refresh, cut the glyph hamster down to head, two ears and body (no feet or tail) at 16/18px, and use the app's shocked-hamster silhouette as the time's-up tray state.

evaluations.verdict: The single most joyful motion in the set is implied here (spin, slow, land with a bounce, burst of confetti), and teachers would know the randomiser card at a glance. As a mark it underdelivers: the winning chip holds a black bar that reads as a minus sign or a redaction, the timer (the headline widget) is absent, it shrinks to a pink rectangle with a dash at 16px, and the crisp, pixel-aligned glyph reads as a server, a list or a Control Center toggle rather than a slot machine.
evaluations.riff: Put a shape in the winning chip instead of a black bar (land the reel on the hamster's head, or a star), which kills the minus-sign read and ties the name picker to the brand's mascot.

evaluations.verdict: Two real widgets set side by side rather than one idea: ring and traffic light compete, the true conic gradient makes the ring read as a colour-picker wheel, and there is no single silhouette to reduce, so at true 1x the glyph reads as the characters 'O8' and the lamps blur into a 2px stub at 16px. As a system, its two motions (lamps changing, ring draining) would pull against each other.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and give the ring's true timer.tsx conic gradient to master or diecut; that gradient is the one genuinely app-faithful thing this concept found.

evaluations.verdict: The cleanest small-size performer: at 16/32px it's a bright ring on a white sticker, and on the amber canvas it looks exactly like a timer sticker slapped on the board, which suggests a sticker family for every widget plus slap-on and peel-off motion. But the 15° tilt is invisible on a circle, so its one sticker gesture is lost; the icon is a generic progress ring, and the solid-disc glyph with a blob-shaped hole reads as an eyeball or eclipse at 16px.
evaluations.riff: Make the sticker gesture visible by peeling the die-cut up where time has been spent (a small curl at upper-left). That gives the static icon a gesture and the system a natural peel/slap launch motion, and the glyph can take master's notch in place of the blob-shaped hole.

general: Seven of nine concepts are the same rainbow ring on an amber plate, which is right for recognition, but every sheet is still judged as a single frame: nobody rendered the moves that make a timer app's mark special, such as the tray glyph draining at true 16/18px, a countdown favicon, a loading loop, a time's-up state or an empty state. The best concepts are really states of one system: master's notched die-cut ring as the scalable mark and live glyph, mascot's hamster-at-home as the idle hero and empty-state performer, hamcap's rider pose as the running/loading animation, and starcap's star as the finish-line pop. Next round should build that merged system and prove it with true-1x state strips, keeping idle glyphs as closed shapes (open arcs read as refresh, and dashed rings read as loading). It should also settle the palette, since the flat hard-joined bands read as a donut chart while the app's ring is a continuous conic gradient (only ringplus used it), and show the layered macOS 26 tinted/clear appearances, which no sheet covers.

evaluations.verdict: This is the strongest of the pure-ring systems: it stays bold at 32/16 and the silhouette really is closed. But at true 1x the notch is a one-pixel wobble, so the tray mark is just a lumpy donut. In colour, flat Google-like primary bands forming a C sit close to the Google colour-ring family (the G, Google One, Chrome) in a teacher's tab strip, and the rainbow, its only recogniser, disappears in macOS 26 Tinted/Clear.
evaluations.riff: Swap the Google-like primaries for the app's warmer sticker rainbow (coral, tangerine, marigold, leaf, sky, violet). At glyph sizes, widen the notch to a pixel-snapped 2px gap so the tray mark reads as time spent, not a donut.

evaluations.verdict: The most literal portrait of the real timer widget, using the app's hamster art verbatim (hamster rule respected), but it falls apart fastest: the rider is a smudge at 64px and gone at 32, and in the tray the thin ring with a lump at 7 o'clock reads as a fishbowl. It also hands critics the 'hamster on a wheel' burnout idiom, on a product for teachers.
evaluations.riff: Merge with mascot: scale the hamster up to mascot size and thicken the ring to master's weight so the rider survives down to 32px. Keep the thin-ring rider pose only for the 512-1024px hero render.

evaluations.verdict: The best-reading ring glyph at true size, but only because the star shrinks to a nub, which turns it into a generic stopwatch (and, at a glance on a tray, a power button). The glossy emoji-style gold star is not the app's flat orange sticker and will date, and a full hard-banded ring around an empty centre is Google One without the '1'.
evaluations.riff: Replace the glossy gold star with the app's own flat orange die-cut star at about twice the size, breaking the rim at 1 o'clock. Put it on master's notched ring so the icon stops reading as Google One with a star, and the glyph gets a second cue beyond the stopwatch nub.

evaluations.verdict: At true 1x the glyph is a dashed circle, the universal loading/busy sign (GNOME's process-working icon, the Windows spinner, Linear's backlog status), which is the worst thing a tray icon can say. In colour, pink/orange/yellow/green/blue capsules with one empty slot read as a Trivial Pursuit piece missing a wedge, and under deuteranopia the spent socket cannot be told apart from the pink and green blocks, so the 'one spent' story collapses.
evaluations.riff: Close the gaps into seams so it becomes one continuous chunky ring whose only gap is the spent block (in effect master's notch). Keep blocks going out one by one only as the live tray state while a timer runs, never as the idle brand glyph.

evaluations.verdict: This is the calm brand direction the client already called uninspired, in colours teachers never see in the app. The deep sage-teal leading cap nearly vanishes into the deep sage plate, the amber-to-sage stretch turns khaki, and a muted gradient ring on dark green is the wellness/fintech cliché, which for deuteranopes flattens to a single grey.
evaluations.riff: Retire it as a standalone concept and use the sage palette as master's macOS dark/tinted variant, on a lighter sage plate so the leading cap keeps its contrast.

evaluations.verdict: The only truly ownable mark: the app's hamster, used verbatim (hamster rule respected), cannot be mistaken for any Google, Apple or Meta ring, and it survives macOS 26 Tinted mode and deuteranopia better than any ring. The glyph is the weak link: at 16-18px the two knocked-out eyes in a round blob read as a skull, ghost or bug, the head with two round ears edges toward a Mickey-style three-circle cluster, and the open 250-degree arc reads as a reload arrow.
evaluations.riff: Draw a purpose-built glyph: side profile, one ear, no eye knockouts, the curly tail as the signature, sitting inside master's closed notched ring instead of an open arc. That removes the skull, Mickey and reload reads and keeps the one asset nobody else owns.

evaluations.verdict: The crispest, best pixel-snapped glyph in the set, but it says filing cabinet, server rack or a menu in a box, not name picker, and it drops the rainbow timer the client named first. At 16px the single dark dash on a lilac-pink-butter window reads as a minus or no-entry sign inside an Instagram-style gradient square, and slot-reel imagery is an avoidable gambling association for school buyers.
evaluations.riff: Let the chosen-name chip overhang the frame on both sides and split it into two uneven word-bars. The silhouette then becomes unique (no longer a cabinet) and the centre reads as a name, not a minus.

evaluations.verdict: At true size the traffic-light pill turns into an '8', so the tray mark reads 'O8' right next to the clock: an accidental numeral that breaks the spirit of the client's rule, from two widgets that never merge into one idea. In the Dock the smooth full-spectrum ring is the macOS beach ball, and it is the 2024-26 AI-halo/Instagram-ring cliché, so this is the concept most likely to look dated by 2029.
evaluations.riff: Drop the traffic light and flatten the hue wheel into warm solid bands. What remains is master, so fold it in.

evaluations.verdict: Its one idea, the 15-degree tilt, is invisible because a rotated circle looks the same. What remains is a big white disc with a colour ring, the most Chrome/Google One-like favicon in the set, and the glyph is a heavy donut with a lumpy hole (Cortana's old ring on a Windows taskbar), while the disc squeezes the amber plate down to a thin frame.
evaluations.riff: Give the sticker a non-circular die-cut (the border following the caps as in master, or a peeled corner) so the sticker and the tilt can actually be seen, and shrink the disc to about 70% of the plate.

general: Seven of nine concepts are the same rainbow ring on the same amber plate, and at 16px master, diecut, starcap and hamcap all shrink to 'a multicolour ring around a light centre'. That is the Google colour-ring family (Chrome, Google One, the G) already in every teacher's tab strip beside Google Classroom. No version of the rainbow is safe: six flat bands read as Google One or the six-stripe Pride flag, and the smooth conic gradient reads as the macOS beach ball, the AI halo or the Instagram story ring, so the rainbow has to become the supporting colour of a shape the client owns, not the identity itself. The tray glyphs come down to generic system shapes (donut, spinner, stopwatch, 'O8', filing cabinet); the only ownable subject is the hamster, and nobody has yet drawn a purpose-built 16px profile silhouette of it (one ear, curly tail, no eye knockouts). Nothing was checked in macOS 26 Clear/Tinted modes or for colour-vision deficiency, both of which strip the rainbow; in my simulation only mascot, starcap and reel kept their identity. Round 4 should anchor on the hamster, warm the rainbow away from Google's primaries, drop the dated gloss (star, traffic light), and screen finalists against Google One, Chrome, Meta AI, Instagram and Disney before anything goes to the client.
